ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle, B is at the lower left and is the right-angle vertex, AB is vertical upward, BC is horizontal to the right, and AC is the hypotenuse; crosses are drawn inside the triangular region, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward. Reasoning: establish a coordinate system, take B=(0,0), take BC as the positive direction of the x-axis and AB as the positive direction of the y-axis, and let AB=BC=L. Then the interior of the triangle satisfies x≥0, y≥0, x+y≤L, and side AC is x+y=L. A positive ion enters from B along the direction BC, that is, the initial velocity is along the +x direction; the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward, and from the direction of the Lorentz force it can be known that the ion undergoes counterclockwise uniform circular motion. The angular velocity is ω=qB/m, the radius is R=mv/(qB), and the trajectory can be written as x=R sin(ωt), y=R[1−cos(ωt)]. If the ion exits from side AC, then when it first touches AC it should satisfy x+y=L, that is, R[sinθ+1−cosθ]=L, where θ=ωt. Let f(θ)=sinθ+1−cosθ. Within 0≤θ≤π, f'(θ)=cosθ+sinθ, and f'(θ)=0 gives θ=3π/4; therefore f first increases and then decreases, with the maximum point at θ=3π/4. Since exiting from AC must occur when the ion first reaches boundary AC from inside the triangle, and the first reaching of AC can only occur in the increasing stage of f, the time for exiting from AC must satisfy θ≤3π/4, that is, t≤3πm/(4qB). Therefore, if the motion time of the ion in the magnetic field is greater than 3πm/(4qB), it will not exit from side AC.

Since exiting from AC must occur when the ion first reaches boundary AC from inside the triangle, and the first reaching of AC can only occur in the increasing stage of f, the time for exiting from AC must satisfy θ≤3π/4, that is, t≤3πm/(4qB). Therefore, if the motion time of the ion in the magnetic field is greater than 3πm/(4qB), it will not exit from side AC.
